title: New license request: GNAT-exception
body:
**1.** License Name: none
**2.** Short identifier: GMGPL-exception
**3.** License Author or steward: Presumably someone on the GNAT team at New York University, who may or may not work at Adacore now.
**4.** Comments: Fedora license exception review: https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/issues/142

GPL 2 with this exception is known as the GNAT modified GPL or GMGPL. The exception by itself has no name that I'm aware of. As far as I can tell it originated when GNAT (the GNU NYU Ada Translator) was written at New York University. Adacore once used GMGPL for all their Ada libraries. It's much rarer now, as they have moved most of their code to GPL 3 and the GCC Runtime Library exception. I'm currently aware of two places where this exception is still used:

· Florist still has the old GMGPL – GPL 2 with this exception.

· GPRbuild includes some example code that we install as documentation in Fedora. In recent versions those files apply this exception to GPL 3.
**5.** License Request Url: http://tools.spdx.org/app/license_requests/200
**6.** URL(s): An example chosen at random: https://github.com/AdaCore/florist/blob/master/libsrc/posix-configurable_file_limits.adb

title: New license request: "GStreamer proprietary plugins" exception
body:
A bit of background. GNOME Videos (né "totem") is a video player for the GNOME desktop environment licensed under the GPL v2+. It uses GStreamer (LGPLv2.1+) for video playback. As was, and still is, the case, a number of video codecs are patent encumbered and can't be shipped easily in some places.

That's the reason why there are proprietary video decoding plugins available from various vendors, and which totem would like to use without causing problems by recombining, or shipping together, a GPL totem with non-free GStreamer plugins.

In 2005, we added this note to the COPYING file in totem:
```
The Totem project hereby grant permission for non-gpl compatible GStreamer
plugins to be used and distributed together with GStreamer and Totem. This
permission are above and beyond the permissions granted by the GPL license
Totem is covered by.
```

This better version was added to the Rhythmbox music player in 2008 and is a bit clearer:
```
The Rhythmbox authors hereby grant permission for non-GPL compatible
GStreamer plugins to be used and distributed together with GStreamer and 
Rhythmbox. This permission is above and beyond the permissions granted by
the GPL license by which Rhythmbox is covered. If you modify this code, you may 
extend this exception to your version of the code, but you are not obligated 
to do so. If you do not wish to do so, delete this exception statement from 
your version.
```

This exception is also used by GNOME Music, and mentioned in GStreamer's licensing documentation:
https://gstreamer.freedesktop.org/documentation/frequently-asked-questions/licensing.html?gi-language=c#licensing-of-applications-using-gstreamer

title: What license identifier can be used for LZMA SDK?
body:

https://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html

I can find an LZMA-Exception identifier, which looks like its purpose is for NSIS rather than the LZMA SDK itself:
https://spdx.org/licenses/LZMA-exception.html

I've taken a look at:
https://wiki.spdx.org/view/Legal_Team/Decisions/Dealing_with_Public_Domain_within_SPDX_Files_(DRAFT)

However it is unclear (to me) as to whether we should be creating a new identifier for the LZMA SDK license text, which reads:

```

LZMA SDK is written and placed in the public domain by Igor Pavlov.

Some code in LZMA SDK is based on public domain code from another developers:

Anyone is free to copy, modify, publish, use, compile, sell, or distribute the
```
